title: How to Prepare a Batch of Social Media Content
h1: How to prepare a batch of social media content
description: Plan a month of social posts with a freelancer: pick themes, gather brand assets, write a simple calendar, set review steps and avoid common mistakes.
intro: Posting on social media one day at a time is tiring, and it shows in rushed, inconsistent posts. Ordering a batch of content, such as a month of designed posts with captions, gives you a steady feed and a consistent look. It works best when you prepare the themes, assets and review steps before the designer or writer starts. This article explains how.

faq.q: How many posts should one batch include?
faq.a: Match it to how often you can realistically post. A batch for two to four weeks is a good start because you can learn from it before ordering more.

faq.q: Do I need both a designer and a writer?
faq.a: Not always. Some freelancers do both. If captions matter a lot for your audience, a separate copywriter can be worth it.

faq.q: Should the freelancer post for me?
faq.a: Only if posting is part of the agreed service. If so, give them a limited role in your account or scheduling tool rather than your password.
Usually yes, if the agreement gives you the rights. Ask for editable templates so you can update text and images yourself.

faq.q: How do I keep the posts on brand?
faq.a: Share your logo, colors, fonts and a few example posts you like, and approve the first two or three designs before the rest are made.
